Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we covered
- High level: FinApps wants a low-latency, cost-predictable embedding + retrieval pipeline for customer support search and a small set of single-turn generation endpoints for automated replies.
- Integration targets: TypeScript frontend (edge calls), Python backend (batch embedding + reranker), and on-prem connector for sensitive data.

Action items / next steps
1) Engineering workshop: schedule with Marcus + Dev to walk the SDK quickstart and go over auth, routing and structured-output/tool-calling. (Marcus will propose times)
2) Share sample SDK quickstart artifacts: I attached a zip with Python/TS quickstarts, and Marcus will follow up with an architecture diagram and sample snippets.
3) Security questionnaire & compliance ask: you requested SSO/KMS answers; attached a short PDF and we can set up a compliance call if needed.

Practical notes for your engineers (short)
- SDKs: our Python and TypeScript SDKs support environment-auth via REDWOOD_API_KEY (set as env var) or a short-lived token flow for browser clients.
- Routing: requests can include an X-Redwood-Routing header to prefer low-latency nodes or lower-cost model variants; we can provide an example for the front-end router.
- Embeddings + rerankers: recommend using our embeddings endpoint to generate vectors, store them in your vector DB (we saw you use Pinecone), and call our reranker endpoint for candidate scoring when you need reordering at query time.
- Structured output & tool calling: the SDK supports function/tool calling with a structured JSON schema enforcement mode — useful for extracting intents or calling downstream APIs safely.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (Python + TS samples), security-answers.pdf

If that all sounds good I'll have Marcus propose two slots later this week for the engineering workshop.

Thanks,

Alex / Priya — hi, Marcus from Solutions Engineering here. 

Quick answers + what I'll cover in the workshop:

1) Embeddings + reranker flow- Our recommended pattern: call the embeddings endpoint to get vectors for documents (batch job). At query time, generate the query embedding and use your vector DB to fetch top-K candidates. Then call our /reranker endpoint with the original query + candidate snippets. The reranker accepts raw text + optional precomputed embeddings; we can accept the query embedding if you want to avoid an extra model call. Example header: 

// pseudo
POST /v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: { query: "...", candidates: [{id: "c1", text: "...", embedding: [..optional..]}] }

If you supply query embedding we skip the small embedding call server-side, so you only pay for one embedding generation (the batch doc embeddings) and reranker compute.

2) TypeScript browser auth- We support a short-lived token exchange: your backend mints a limited-scope token (5–15m TTL) using the REDWOOD_API_KEY and returns it to the browser. The browser uses the short token for calls that are safe to expose (e.g., inference with strict rate limits and model constraints). We will share the sample endpoint in the quickstart. Avoid shipping REDWOOD_API_KEY to the client.

3) Structured output / tool calling- The SDK exposes a JSON schema mode that validates model responses against a declared schema and optionally canonicalizes fields. Example: 

expected_schema = {"type":"object","properties": {"action": {"type":"string"}, "amount":{"type":"number"}}} 

When using the function-calling mode the model is asked to return only the JSON for the declared function; SDK will raise a validation error if the output doesn't match. This is how we recommend wiring up downstream calls (safe, deterministic).

Attachments I added: integration-diagram.png (high level flow for edge/browser + backend + vector DB + reranker), redwood-sample-snippets.txt (short code snippets for Python/TS). Also included a checklist for local testing (unit tests for schema validation, sandbox keys, and request replay).
